name: Fossil Workshops (Erfoud)
hero_subtitle: In-town ateliers where Tafilalet stone is cut, polished and turned into ammonites you can hold.

overview.title: Why Erfoud is the fossil capital
overview.p1: The plateaus around Erfoud once lay under a shallow sea. Workshops in town slice dark limestone to reveal ammonites, trilobites and orthoceras, then polish the stone for display and sale.
overview.p2: An atelier visit is the most direct way to understand the craft: from rough block to finished plate. Some places combine a small museum space with the workshop floor.
overview.p3: Buy from clear, established showrooms. Ask about export rules before taking large specimens home.

1.title: Choosing a workshop
1.desc: Prefer places that show the cutting process, not only a souvenir shelf. Hotels often know established names.

2.title: Buying fossils
2.desc: Compare quality and price. Small polished pieces travel easily; large slabs need packing and may face export limits.

3.title: In your day plan
3.desc: Pair with the town centre the same morning or afternoon — no long transfer needed.

gyg.subtitle: Desert day trips use desert roads.

q1.question: Are the fossils real?
q1.answer: Yes — local marine fossils in limestone. Quality and finishing vary by workshop.

q2.question: Can I take them abroad?
q2.answer: Small tourist pieces are commonly sold for export; large or rare specimens may be restricted. Ask before buying.

q3.question: Is entry free?
q3.answer: Browsing a showroom is often free; a formal museum room may charge a small fee.

q4.question: How long?
q4.answer: 45 to 90 minutes including explanations and shopping.

q5.question: Is this only in Erfoud?
q5.answer: Erfoud is the classic town for workshops — in-town ateliers are its signature stop.
